- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 5 days of a new 30-day forecast horizon; add 0.3–0.8% to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags; delay upward adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to ignore it; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent underestimation.
